name: orb_momentum_v32
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: When NIFTY compresses into a 30-minute rolling range (defined by the highest high and lowest low of the past 360 5-second bars), opposing institutional limit orders accumulate at both boundaries, creating a temporarily balanced book. A close above the rolling high for 3 consecutive 5-second bars — confirmed by the index trading above session VWAP — indicates that net buy-side flow has absorbed all resting supply at the range ceiling; the executing TWAP/VWAP order is typically only 40-60% filled and must continue buying, driving 15-25 spot point continuation. Unlike the fixed 09:15-09:35 opening range (orb_v22), this rolling range fires throughout the session, capturing afternoon re-accumulation breakouts that develop after news digestion or FII second-wave entries — a mechanistically distinct signal from the morning institutional calibration breakout.

indicators.name: rolling_high_360
indicators.purpose: 30-minute rolling highest high (360 bars at 5s). Original used 21 bars × 5-min = 105 minutes, but that is too long for a 30-120 second hold — it creates a stale reference level from mid-morning when the breakout fires in the afternoon. Compressed to 30 minutes because (1) NIFTY consolidations relevant to 5s breakout trades form in 15-45 min windows, and (2) 30 min is long enough to act as a meaningful range context filter without referencing price action from >2 hours ago. This is NOT a fixed opening range — it is a live, rolling reference that updates each bar.

indicators.name: rolling_low_360
indicators.purpose: Mirror of rolling_high_360 for bearish breakdown signals. Same 30-minute window rationale — captures the most recent consolidation floor relevant to the current breakout thesis.

indicators.name: vwap
indicators.formula: cumsum(typical_price * volume) / cumsum(volume), reset per day
indicators.purpose: Cumulative session VWAP — no lookback scaling needed. Used as trend context filter: a rolling-range breakout above VWAP confirms that buy-side institutional participants are net long for the session. A breakout above rolling_high but below VWAP would face VWAP-benchmarked supply overhang and is excluded.

indicators.name: persist_3bar
indicators.purpose: 15-second persistence filter — mandatory at 5s resolution. NIFTY index microstructure produces frequent 1-2 bar transient spikes above/below rolling range boundaries that immediately retrace, driven by large single-lot market orders. Original 5-min bars naturally filtered these sub-5-minute spikes. Three consecutive 5s closes above the range (15 seconds) confirms that the breakout is not a transient spike.

indicators.name: vol_ratio_120
indicators.purpose: 10-minute rolling volume ratio. Original used SMA(volume, 10) on 5-min bars = 50-minute window; compressed to 120 bars (10 min) at 5s because a 50-min volume average would incorporate pre-open and gap-fill periods that distort the intraday baseline. 10-min window gives a recent, session-representative volume norm. Ratio > 1.2 confirms genuine breakout activity, not thin-market drift.

conditions: close > rolling_high_360 for 3 consecutive bars (persist_3bar bullish)
close > vwap (session trend confirms net buy-side)
buy_ce.confirmation: 3-bar persistence above 30-min rolling high + VWAP + volume surge

conditions: close < rolling_low_360 for 3 consecutive bars (persist_3bar bearish)
close < vwap (session trend confirms net sell-side)
buy_pe.confirmation: 3-bar persistence below 30-min rolling low + VWAP + volume surge

exit.stop_rationale: 4 option points = ~8 NIFTY spot points at delta 0.5. Rolling range breakouts from 30-minute consolidations typically throwback 6-10 spot points before continuation or failure; if price retreats more than 8 spot points post-breakout the range has reasserted itself and the thesis is wrong. Tighter than fixed-ORB v22 (5 pts) because rolling range breakouts carry less volatility expansion than morning ORB breakouts.
exit.target_rationale: 6 option points = ~12 NIFTY spot points. Afternoon rolling-range breakouts on NIFTY extend 15-25 spot points on average — shorter than morning ORB's 20-40 points because ambient momentum is lower and liquidity thinner. 12 pts captures the lower 50% of expected continuation (risk:reward = 1:1.5), calibrated to avoid overstaying a move that is already half-done.
exit.eod_rule: flatten at 14:30 IST — rolling range breakouts after 14:30 face thinning liquidity and converging session VWAP that suppresses further continuation

filters.vix_filter: none — rolling range breakouts work in both high and low VIX; VIX filter not present in original and edge is not demonstrably VIX-regime dependent
filters.time_filter: 09:35-14:30 IST; first 20 minutes excluded to let rolling range window populate with 360 bars, cutoff at 14:30 to avoid low-volume late-session noise
filters.volume_filter: volume > 1.2x rolling 10-min average as breakout confirmation
filters.trend_filter: VWAP — price must be on the correct side of session VWAP for the breakout direction
filters.spread_filter: none — limit order execution, no spread cost

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium-high — rolling range breakouts are mechanically simpler than fixed ORB and more susceptible to being front-run by HFT as they watch the same rolling highs/lows. VWAP+volume filter provides some protection against fakeouts but not against adversarial anticipation.

adaptation_notes: Original trades nifty200 stocks on 5-min bars with a rolling 21-bar highest-high/lowest-low (= 105-minute window). Conversion: (1) Applied to NIFTY index — indices have cleaner rolling ranges because they aggregate multi-stock flow, reducing single-stock noise that creates false breakouts. (2) Rolling window compressed from 105 min to 30 min (360 bars) because at 5s resolution we're catching the breakout in real-time and need a recent range reference, not a 2-hour-old one. (3) Fixed opening range NOT used — this strategy's thesis is about ROLLING range breakouts throughout the day, deliberately differentiated from orb_momentum_v22 which uses the static 09:15-09:35 range. (4) Added 3-bar persistence filter (mandatory at 5s, absent in original 5-min). (5) ATR-based stops replaced with fixed 4-pt option premium stop calibrated to typical NIFTY rolling-range throwback depth. (6) Volume window compressed from SMA(volume,10) on 5-min to 120-bar (10-min) on 5s — same real-time window, same purpose.
weaknesses: Rolling range is the same price level every participant watches — highly susceptible to fakeout-and-fade by HFT when range is well-defined
3-bar filter adds 15-second entry lag; fast breakouts will have moved 8-12 spot points before entry fires
Low trade frequency in trending days where range doesn't reform after first breakout
Rolling window crosses day boundaries at open — first 30 min of each session has incomplete range context
Volume filter may be overly tight in low-activity afternoon sessions (post-13:30) where average volume drops significantly
